literature: Wörthmüller 1955: 406-07; Langwill 1980: 45; Lane 1982: 183; SmithD 1989: 32; Waterhouse 1993: 102; Wackernagel 1999: 62; MyersH 2010.
remarks: Wörthmüller 1955 and Waterhouse 1993 both identify the instrument as a tenor. Wörthmüller gives A for the pitch. Wörthmüller is usually Wörthmüller is usually a credible witness, and one therefore wonders if the instrument has been altered substantially since he saw it in the early 1950s. MyersH 2010 says the instrument is a cut-down bass. Excellent workmanship. 15 ferrules with rings, engraved zigzag stripes in three-cornered field, bow-shaped indentations, and cast points, perforated with holes, on the borders, dragon-scale pattern. Moveable slide-stay flat, with hinges decorated with cast angel’s heads on the proximal side, hole where a handle was once attached, musician with tenor viola da gamba on one surface and a winged form with a lute on the reverse. Immoveable slide-stay missing. Small dents in slide-bow; twisted wire ring in slide-bow, mounted on saddle with zigzag pattern. Flat slide-stay, with decorations matching slide-stay; eyelet on bell-pipe side; hinge with pin, fastened on bell-pipe side to saddle similar to that in slide-bow. Secondary coil of tubing in bell sec., with tuning slide attached to push-rod, which passes through an articulated columnar stay. Main bell-bow has ring attached to saddle. Secondary slide-bow has similar saddle, to which the push-rod is attached, and a bumper guard; on this bumper guard are mounted five animal figures. Bell has modest terminal flare. Garland is narrow, plain on proximal border; narrow rim-wire.
